CAMPUS INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY & SCIENCE
OFFICE OF THE DEAN (ACADEMIC AFFAIRS)
DOCUMENT NO: ACAD-REG-2025/V4
DATE: JUNE 15, 2025

ACADEMIC REGULATIONS 2025–26 FOR UNDERGRADUATE & POSTGRADUATE PROGRAMS

Section 1: General Preamble
These academic regulations govern all students enrolled in B.Tech, M.Tech, MCA, and Ph.D. programs for the academic year 2025–26. All students are required to maintain high standards of academic integrity and adhere strictly to the rules formulated by the Academic Council.

chunks.section: Section 4: Course Registration and Minimum Credits
chunks.content:
Section 4: Course Registration and Minimum Credits
4.1 Every student must register for a minimum of 18 credits and a maximum of 26 credits in any regular semester.
4.2 Dropping a registered course is permitted within the first two weeks of semester commencement subject to Dean approval.
4.3 Add-on honors or minor degree tracks require a cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 7.50 or higher with zero backlogs at the end of the 4th semester.

Section: Attendance Requirements
Clause 5.1: Mandatory Minimum Attendance
Every candidate must secure a minimum aggregate attendance of 75% in each course registered in the semester to be eligible to appear for the End Semester Examinations.

chunks.section: Clause 5.3: Detention Due to Attendance Shortage
chunks.content:

Clause 5.2: Condonation of Attendance Shortage
Condonation of shortage of attendance between 65% and 74% may be granted by the College Academic Committee on genuine medical grounds (hospitalization supported by a valid certificate from a Registered Medical Practitioner) or due to officially approved participation in university/national-level sports and technical events.
A prescribed condonation fee of INR 1,500 per subject must be remitted prior to the hall ticket issuance.

Clause 5.3: Detention Due to Attendance Shortage
Candidates securing less than 65% attendance in aggregate or in individual mandatory laboratory/practical courses will NOT be eligible for condonation under any circumstances. Such candidates shall be declared detained (short of attendance) and must repeat the semester in the subsequent academic year.

Section 6: Grading System and Evaluation Scheme
Clause 6.1: Letter Grades and Grade Points
The institution follows a 10-point absolute grading scale:
• Grade O (Outstanding): 90–100 marks, Grade Point: 10
• Grade A+ (Excellent): 80–89 marks, Grade Point: 9
• Grade A (Very Good): 70–79 marks, Grade Point: 8
• Grade B+ (Good): 60–69 marks, Grade Point: 7
• Grade B (Above Average): 55–59 marks, Grade Point: 6
• Grade C (Pass): 50–54 marks, Grade Point: 5
• Grade F (Fail): Below 50 marks, Grade Point: 0

• Grade F (Fail): Below 50 marks, Grade Point: 0
Clause 6.2: Pass Criteria
A student is declared to have passed a theory course if they score at least 45% in the End Semester Examination and a minimum aggregate of 50% combined across Continuous Assessment and End Semester Exam.

OFFICE OF THE CHIEF WARDEN - RESIDENTIAL CAMPUS
HOSTEL RULES & STUDENT CODE OF CONDUCT MANUAL (2025-26)

Section 1: General Residency Guidelines
All residential blocks (Boys Hostel Blocks A, B, C and Girls Hostel Blocks Pearl and Jasmine) operate under the direct oversight of the Chief Warden and Resident Wardens. Peaceful living, mutual respect, and adherence to hostel decorum are mandatory.

chunks.section: Clause 3.2: Night-Out and Weekend Leave Pass Procedure
chunks.content:
Section: Timings and Night Passes
Clause 3.1: Campus and Hostel Gate Curfew
The main college gate and all residential hostel entrance doors shall be locked strictly at 8:30 PM on all days including weekends.
All hostel residents must scan their RFID biometric student ID at the biometric turnstile before 8:30 PM.
Arrival after 8:30 PM without prior written warden sanction incurs a disciplinary late slip. Accumulating three late slips in a semester will result in suspension of hostel privileges.

chunks.content:

Clause 3.2: Night-Out and Weekend Leave Pass Procedure
Hostel students who wish to stay outside campus overnight or travel home during weekends must apply via the CampusIQ Smart Resident Portal at least 24 hours in advance.
The night-out pass application requires verified SMS/email consent from the registered parent/guardian.
Students must produce the generated QR pass to the security gatekeeper when departing and returning.

chunks.section: Section 4: Mess Timings and Dining Hall Regulations
chunks.content:
Section 4: Mess Timings and Dining Hall Regulations
All resident students must strictly observe the dining hall schedule:
• Breakfast: 7:30 AM – 9:00 AM (Weekdays) | 8:00 AM – 9:30 AM (Sundays)
• Lunch: 12:30 PM – 2:00 PM
• Evening Snacks: 5:00 PM – 6:00 PM
• Dinner: 7:30 PM – 9:15 PM

Taking food items, crockery, or utensils out of the dining hall into hostel rooms is strictly prohibited. Outside commercial food delivery (Zomato/Swiggy) is permitted at the Main Security Gate only until 8:15 PM.

chunks.section: Section 5: Strict Anti-Ragging and Zero-Tolerance Discipline
chunks.content:
Section 5: Strict Anti-Ragging and Zero-Tolerance Discipline
Clause 5.1: Zero Tolerance on Ragging
Ragging in any form—physical, psychological, verbal, or digital—is a cognizable penal offense under UGC Regulations 2009 and the Supreme Court mandate. Any resident student found indulging in ragging will be immediately expelled from the college and handed over to law enforcement.
Emergency Helpline: Anti-Ragging Cell +91-98765-00001 (Available 24x7).

CENTRE FOR CAREER EXCELLENCE & PLACEMENTS
CAMPUS PLACEMENT AND INTERNSHIP POLICY (2025–2026 BATCH)

Section 1: Vision and Student Commitment
The Placement Cell strives to provide equal and transparent recruitment opportunities for all eligible students. Registering with the Placement Portal signifies acceptance of all operational rules.

chunks.section: Clause 4.2: Dream Offer and Super Dream Upgrades
chunks.content:
Section: Job Offer Policies
Clause 4.1: The One-Student-One-Job Policy
To ensure fair placement opportunities across the entire student batch, the college enforces a strict 'One-Student-One-Job' policy.
Once a student secures a confirmed job offer from a visiting company, they are considered placed and are automatically de-registered from attending further recruitment drives, subject to the Dream Offer exception below.

chunks.section: Clause 4.2: Dream Offer and Super Dream Upgrades
chunks.content:
d are automatically de-registered from attending further recruitment drives, subject to the Dream Offer exception below.
Clause 4.2: Dream Offer and Super Dream Upgrades
A placed student is allowed to apply for a 'Dream Company' or 'Super Dream Company' recruitment drive under the following conditions:
• If the current job offer CTC is below INR 7.0 LPA, the student can sit for Dream Companies offering CTC of INR 12.0 LPA or higher (at least 1.7x increase).
• If the current job offer is between INR 7.0 LPA and 12.0 LPA, the student can attempt Super Dream drives offering CTC exceeding INR 20.0 LPA.
A maximum of ONE upgrade offer is permitted.

Section 5: Placement Eligibility Criteria and Minimum Cut-Offs
Clause 5.1: Minimum Academic Requirements
• Minimum CGPA of 6.50 (or 65% aggregate equivalent) with NO active standing backlogs at the time of company registration.
• A maximum of two cleared historical backlogs is permitted by most Tier-1 recruiters.
• Minimum 75% attendance in mandatory Soft Skills, Aptitude, and Mock Interview training sessions conducted in the 6th and 7th semesters.

Clause 5.2: Full-Semester 8th Semester Industry Internship
Students who receive a 6-month pre-placement internship offer from recognized tech companies are granted an Academic On-Duty waiver for the 8th semester, provided they complete their final capstone project with their company mentor and submit monthly progress reports.

DIRECTORATE OF STUDENT WELFARE
STUDENT LEAVE & ON-DUTY (OD) ATTENDANCE CREDIT REGULATIONS

Section 1: General Attendance Policy
Every lecture, tutorial, and lab class counts toward the mandatory attendance roster. Absence without sanctioned leave will result in an unexcused mark.

Section: On-Duty (OD) Leave Quota and Approval Process
Clause 3.1: Academic and Event On-Duty (OD) Limit
On-Duty (OD) attendance credit is granted to students who represent the college in approved academic symposiums, national hackathons, IEEE conferences, cultural festivals, or university sports tournaments.
The maximum allowable On-Duty (OD) limit is 10 working days per semester.
OD days are counted as present for the purpose of the 75% minimum semester attendance requirement.

Clause 3.2: OD Application Procedure
Students must apply for OD at least 3 days prior to the event through the Student ERP portal with the official invitation brochure and obtain counter-signatures from the Faculty Coordinator and Head of Department (HOD). Post-event attendance certificates must be submitted within 3 days of returning to campus.

Section 4: Medical Leave Policy
Clause 4.1: Procedure for Medical Absence
In the event of sickness or hospitalization exceeding 3 consecutive working days:
1. The student or guardian must notify the Class Mentor and HOD via email within 48 hours of illness onset.
2. Upon return to campus, the student must present a Medical Fitness Certificate issued by a Civil Surgeon or Authorized Medical Officer of an empanelled hospital, along with medical bills, discharge summary, and diagnostic reports to the College Health Centre.

CAMPUS INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY
FINANCIAL AID & SCHOLARSHIP SCHEMES MANUAL (2025–2026)

Section 1: Institutional Commitment to Affordable Education
The institution allocates an annual corpus of INR 2.5 Crores to support meritorious, underprivileged, and sports-achieving students through tuition fee waivers and stipends.

Section: Institutional Merit Scholarships
Clause 2.1: Academic Merit Scholarship
To reward top academic performers, the top 3 students in each engineering branch (based on SGPA in the preceding academic year with zero backlogs) are granted tuition fee waivers:
• 1st Rank: 50% Tuition Fee Concession
• 2nd Rank: 35% Tuition Fee Concession
• 3rd Rank: 20% Tuition Fee Concession

rs:
• 1st Rank: 50% Tuition Fee Concession
• 2nd Rank: 35% Tuition Fee Concession
• 3rd Rank: 20% Tuition Fee Concession
Clause 2.2: Merit-cum-Means (MCM) Scholarship
Students with a family annual gross income below INR 2,50,000 (INR 2.5 LPA) and who have maintained a minimum CGPA of 7.0 with no standing backlogs are eligible for a 40% tuition fee waiver.
Required documents: Income Certificate issued by Revenue Tahsildar, latest Ration Card/Aadhaar, and bank account statement.

Section 3: Sports Excellence Concession
Students who have represented the state or nation in recognized Olympic sports or AIU inter-university tournaments receive a 100% tuition and hostel fee waiver along with a specialized nutrition allowance.

Section 4: Application Deadlines and Disqualification
The final deadline to submit scholarship applications for odd and even semesters is August 31, 2025.
Disqualification: Any student found involved in indiscipline, malpractice in exams, or hostel misconduct forfeits all scholarship concessions with immediate effect.

OFFICE OF THE CONTROLLER OF EXAMINATIONS (COE)
EXAMINATION RULES, EVALUATION SCHEME, AND MALPRACTICE CODES

Section 1: Structure of Examination System
The academic performance of students is evaluated based on Continuous Internal Assessment (CIA) carrying 40 marks and End Semester University Examinations (ESE) carrying 60 marks, totaling 100 marks per theory course.

Section: Revaluation and Answer Script Photocopy
Clause 7.1: Application for Revaluation
Students who are not satisfied with their grades in the End Semester Theory Examinations may apply for revaluation within 10 days from the date of declaration of results.
• Fee for Paper Photocopy / Script Review: INR 500 per subject
• Fee for Challenge Revaluation: INR 1,200 per subject

s.
• Fee for Paper Photocopy / Script Review: INR 500 per subject
• Fee for Challenge Revaluation: INR 1,200 per subject
Clause 7.2: Grade Revision Criteria
If the difference between the original marks and the revaluated marks is 5 marks or higher, the revised marks shall be awarded. If the difference is 15 marks or higher, the answer script will be submitted to a third evaluator whose decision shall be final.

Section 8: Examination Malpractice Penalties
Clause 8.1: Unfair Means & Electronic Devices
Possession of mobile phones, smartwatches, programmable calculators, or handwritten chits in the examination hall, whether used or not, constitutes severe malpractice.
Penalty:
• Possession of unauthorized material: Cancellation of the examination of that particular course and an 'F' grade awarded.
• Copying or assisting others: Cancellation of all registered courses of the ongoing semester and debarment for one subsequent semester.

SPORTS & CULTURAL EXCELLENCE SCHOLARSHIP AND ATTENDANCE CONCESSION POLICY

Section 1: Purpose and Objectives
The institution is committed to promoting extracurricular excellence in national and international sporting and cultural arenas. This policy outlines fee waivers, special internal examination provisions, and attendance credits.

Section 2: Fee Waiver Categories for Student Athletes
Clause 2.1: International Level Representation
Students representing the country in Olympics, Commonwealth Games, Asian Games, or World Championships receive:
1. 100% Tuition fee waiver for all remaining academic years.
2. Free single-occupancy air-conditioned hostel accommodation and dietary mess allowance.
3. Special sponsorship grant of INR 50,000 per tournament.

Clause 2.2: National and Inter-University Representation
Students winning Gold, Silver, or Bronze medals in All India Inter-University (AIU) tournaments or Khelo India Youth Games receive:
1. 75% Tuition fee waiver.
2. Free boarding in college residential campus.
3. Priority course and lab scheduling.

Section 3: Special Examination Provisions
Clause 3.1: Clash with Examination Schedule
If an officially scheduled tournament or national training camp coincides with Mid-Semester Assessments or End Semester Examinations, the student is permitted to appear for a Special Makeup Examination without penalty or grade cap.
Clause 3.2: Submission Timeline
The student or sports coach must submit official participation documentation to the Controller of Examinations at least 7 days before the exam commencement.
